idiom_name: PriorityQueue or sortedSetOf window under a Mutex, timed with withTimeoutOrNull
implementation_notes: Kotlin adds no resequencer of its own; channels and flows are the transport primitives (the documentation presents Channel as the stream type, and a flow preserves order only while its operators do). The realization pairs an ordered structure on the JVM - java.util.PriorityQueue or sortedSetOf - with a Mutex, uses withTimeoutOrNull or a select with onTimeout for the gap deadline, and hands the ordered run to a Channel. Cold flows fit a single pipeline stage; sharing the ordered result through a SharedFlow is exactly the point after which concurrent collection must not be assumed to preserve order.
pitfalls: withTimeout cancels the coroutine it wraps, not just the wait: run the gap policy in a withTimeoutOrNull branch or a select onTimeout, otherwise a late message cancels the whole stage.
java.util.PriorityQueue is not thread safe and has no remove-by-key, so duplicates, reject-old and capacity eviction need a TreeMap or sortedSetOf with explicit removal.
Fanning a channel out to several consumer coroutines re-parallelises the stream; the resequencer's guarantee holds only up to the first stage that consumes concurrently.
